title: PR212's frame floor on PR217's butterfly word: κ < 6.968e-4 banked, +1.77% of frame room left (no new κ)
body:
**No new κ, no existing file changed.** #212 bounded the bit coarse saving of one word — #200's physical bit word, shared by #205, #206 and #207 — over every admissible choice of operation frames. #217 holds the current record on a **different word**: 440 four-input XOR reassociations (880 graph nodes and scalar controls) on top of #211's cascade frames and #200's construction. This applies #212's method, unchanged, to that word.

## Result

At 1,200 Lagrangian rounds, the round count of #212's published run, on #217's head `b739fc2`:

| Ledger | #200's word (#212) | #217's butterfly word (here) |
|---|---|---|
| own: floor on C | 2,804,210 | 2,800,700 |
| own: coarse < | 6.904e-4 | **6.913e-4** |
| own: κ < | 6.900e-4 | 6.908e-4 |
| completed banks: floor on C | 2,780,144 | 2,776,634 |
| completed banks: coarse < | 6.964e-4 | **6.973e-4** |
| completed banks: κ < | 6.959e-4 | 6.968e-4 |

The like-for-like pair at 400 rounds moves the same way (own 6.909e-4 vs 6.918e-4, banked 6.969e-4 vs 6.978e-4), so the comparison does not depend on the round count.

The word's own numbers, recomputed here from its certificate:

| quantity | #200's word | #217's butterfly word |
|---|---|---|
| certified coarse saving, own | 6.7777395e-4 | 6.7938424e-4 |
| `D/C` of the certified layout, own | 6.7837287e-4 | 6.7998615e-4 |
| certified coarse saving, completed banks | 6.8366e-4 (#207) | 6.8516596e-4 |
| `D/C` of the certified layout, banks | 6.8427e-4 (#207) | 6.8578301e-4 |
| κ of the composition | 6.831904550365e-4 (#207) | 6.84696826673891e-4 |

**The butterflies raised the ceiling and the achieved value by about the same 0.13%, leaving slightly less frame room than before**: +1.68% from the achieved `D/C` to the ceiling here against +1.77% on #200's word, and +1.77% against +1.86% on the κ basis. Reassociation is not a way to enlarge the frame slack; it is a different word with its own, slightly higher, ceiling — which is what #212's scope statement already said.

## How the word was obtained and checked

#217's own `candidate.py` rebuilt the changed word from #202's head `8d8d67b` (fetched from `pull/202/head`), #211's pinned frame payload and the frozen butterfly overlay, checking those hashes itself. The three emitted payloads reproduce #217's declared hashes exactly — `graph_p12.json` `2bb271df…`, `word_p12.json` `ef77a7d3…`, `frames_p12.json` `4e0fce06…` — and the word has 41,288 operations, 18,908 roles, 1,760 reuse pairs, 3,960 gauges and **11,671 changed operation frames**, the number its `expected-bit.json` declares.

`ceiling.py --tree` then passed every self-test on that word: the certified layout lies inside every derived joint bound, **its slot chains reproduce #217's certified ledger child for child** (W 20,668, rank 1,486,160), the terminal record substitutes `[3, 21]` per sink and stage, and every per-slot floor is below its actual chain. Fact 1 reproduces the certificate to eight digits (`6.7938424e-4 < D/C = 6.7998615e-4`, gap 0.089%), matching an independent closed-form computation.

`rebuild_word.py` and `build_tree.py` reproduce the run end to end; the tree's certificate is a shim whose `bit` record is #217's own post-terminal profile plus the pre-sink profile restored by the terminal record, and every field of it is re-derived by #212's own self-tests.

## Added after the first push: what combining PR216's cuts with this word can reach

PR216 (`research/coordinated-crossover-pr200-v2`, head `34abdc5`) is a third layout on the same lineage, keeping PR211's frames and admitting 220 further operation-frame changes (kappa = 6.838643131376e-4). Since this note's ceiling bounds every frame layout of PR217's word, `transfer_check.py` (added in the second commit) settles the structural side of the obvious combination question from the two packages' own words:

* both have **41,288 operations** and identical DAG-fixing records (11,856 arcs, 25,900 order entries, 1,760 reuse pairs, 3,960 gauges, 6,624 root roles, 17,688 phase-1 and 7,728 plain operations, the same 1,760 sources and reads); exactly **880 operation contents** differ -- PR217's reassociation set -- along with 7,068 operation frames;
* PR216's admission records are `[op_index, [basis vectors ...]]` in that same index space: 6,191 current bases, 6,258 override records, 2,268 canonical subspaces, of which only **3 of 6,258** touch a rewritten operation and **none of the 2,268** does;
* so a merge is well defined at the index level, but PR216 admits with the scalar word fixed and PR217's change is exactly there: a merged layout is a new submission needing fresh admission and a fresh column replay;
* and it is capped: any frame layout of this word gives kappa < 6.968e-4, at most **+1.77%** over the 6.84696826673891e-4 record, while PR216's own layout on the plain word sits **0.122% below** it. The bank absorption of #219 (+2.30% over the same record, accounting ledger) is the route this comparison favours.


## Scope

This bounds frame layouts of #217's word only, in the sense #212's floor has. The reassociations are part of the word, so nothing here bounds further reassociation, other circuits, reuse, gauges or sinks — the escapes #212 lists. The pre-sink profile is reconstructed rather than read from #217's receipt (its own `run_bit.py` needs Linux `resource`/`signal.alarm` and pinned numpy 2.3.5 / scipy 1.17.0); the delta is exact and #212's child-for-child self-test is the check. All κ remain conditional on each submission's stated interfaces.

Credits: #212 (Chafik Boukhalfa) for the method and the script, unmodified; #217 (hcg890) for the word and `candidate.py`; #211 (Rohan Arun) for the pinned cascade frames; #200/#168 v4 for the base word and vendored checker. Prepared with Anthropic Claude assistance; Apache-2.0.
